import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker
import numpy as np

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Data Cleaning and Preparation
# Filter out potential outliers or extreme values for better visualization
df_filtered = df[(df['price_usd'] > 100) & (df['price_usd'] < 10000)]
df_filtered = df_filtered[df_filtered['megapixels'] < 80]

# Determine the order of body_type by median price for a more organized plot
body_type_order = df_filtered.groupby('body_type')['price_usd'].median().sort_values(ascending=False).index

# Create the figure and axes
plt.style.use('seaborn-v0_8-whitegrid')
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(14, 10))

# Create the Raincloud plot using a combination of stripplot and violinplot
sns.violinplot(
    data=df_filtered,
    x='price_usd',
    y='body_type',
    order=body_type_order,
    orient='h',
    palette='magma',
    inner=None,  # Remove the inner box/stick from the violin
    linewidth=1.5,
    cut=0, # Don't extend the violin past the data range
    ax=ax
)

sns.stripplot(
    data=df_filtered,
    x='price_usd',
    y='body_type',
    order=body_type_order,
    orient='h',
    size=4,
    color='white',
    edgecolor='gray',
    linewidth=0.5,
    jitter=0.2, # Add jitter to see individual points
    alpha=0.6,
    ax=ax
)

# Add boxplots inside the violins for summary statistics
sns.boxplot(
    data=df_filtered,
    x='price_usd',
    y='body_type',
    order=body_type_order,
    orient='h',
    ax=ax,
    width=0.2,
    boxprops={'zorder': 2, 'facecolor': 'white'},
    medianprops={'color': 'black', 'zorder': 3},
    whiskerprops={'color': 'black', 'zorder': 3},
    capprops={'color': 'black', 'zorder': 3},
    showfliers=False # Hide outlier points as they are shown in the stripplot
)

# Set plot title and labels
ax.set_title('Price Distribution of Digital Cameras by Body Type', fontsize=20, weight='bold', pad=20)
ax.set_xlabel('Price (USD) - Logarithmic Scale', fontsize=12)
ax.set_ylabel('Body Type', fontsize=12)

# Use a log scale for the x-axis to better handle the skewed price data
ax.set_xscale('log')

# Format the x-axis ticks to be more readable (e.g., $1,000)
formatter = mticker.FuncFormatter(lambda x, p: f'${x:,.0f}')
ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(formatter)
ax.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

# Add vertical lines for median price points to aid comparison
median_prices = df_filtered.groupby('body_type')['price_usd'].median().loc[body_type_order]
for i, price in enumerate(median_prices):
    ax.axvline(x=price, color='grey', linestyle='--', linewidth=0.8, ymin=i/len(body_type_order), ymax=(i+1)/len(body_type_order))
    ax.text(price * 1.1, i + 0.3, f'Median: ${price:,.0f}', color='black', ha='left', va='center', fontsize=9, backgroundcolor=(1,1,1,0.6))

# Improve aesthetics
sns.despine(left=True)
ax.grid(axis='x', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)
ax.grid(axis='y', linestyle='', alpha=0)

# Adjust layout
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
